hypothesis: If Darwin is right, no geologically oceanic island or archipelago (volcanic hot-spot island, atoll or intra-oceanic island arc that has never been joined to a continent) has a native amphibian species; every amphibian recorded there is a human introduction.
pass_criterion: Across a pre-registered list of 40 oceanic island units (see planned unit list in interpretation), zero units have an amphibian species that is endemic to the unit by GBIF occurrence data, where 'endemic' means the species has >= 10 non-fossil, non-captive occurrence records worldwide and >= 95 % of them fall inside the unit. An endemic species cannot be a human introduction, so endemism is used as a conservative proof of native status.
fail_criterion: Two or more independent oceanic island units each have at least one endemic amphibian species by the rule above: the universal statement is refuted. Exactly one such unit: 'mixed' (a single counterexample Darwin himself might have disputed, like his New Zealand frog). The proportion of units with native amphibians is reported in either case to characterise the 'general absence' Darwin also asserted.
interpretation: Darwin's 'islands with which the great oceans are studded' is read as geologically oceanic islands, which he distinguishes from continental islands elsewhere in the chapter (he explicitly excludes New Zealand and the Falklands as continental). Batrachians = class Amphibia (GBIF classKey 131). 'Never been found' is read as no native population; introductions, which Darwin himself discusses (Madeira, Azores, Mauritius), are excluded by requiring endemism. Pre-registered oceanic units (ISO code or bounding box): Fiji FJ, Samoa WS, American Samoa AS, Tonga TO, Palau PW, Micronesia FM, Marshall Is. MH, Northern Marianas MP, Guam GU, French Polynesia PF, Cook Is. CK, Vanuatu VU, Niue NU, Tuvalu TV, Kiribati KI, Nauru NR, Wallis & Futuna WF, Tokelau TK, Pitcairn PN, Norfolk I. NF, Bermuda BM, St Helena/Ascension/Tristan SH, Iceland IS, Sao Tome & Principe ST, Cape Verde CV, Comoros KM, Mayotte YT, Mauritius MU, Reunion RE, Christmas I. CX, Cocos (Keeling) CC, Hawaii (box), Galapagos (box), Canary Is. (box), Azores (box), Madeira (box), Juan Fernandez (box), Fernando de Noronha (box), Ogasawara/Bonin (box), Easter I. (box), Lord Howe I. (box). Excluded as continental fragments or shelf islands: New Zealand, Seychelles (granitic), Socotra, New Caledonia, Solomon Is., Bioko, Falklands, Faroes, Japan, Sri Lanka, Madagascar, Taiwan, British Isles, Caribbean Greater Antilles. Classification follows the standard volcanic/arc versus continental distinction used in island biogeography (e.g. Weigelt et al. 2013 PNAS) and is a judgement made before any data were examined.
